articles.summary: Oportunidades estão distribuídas por seis cidades e incluem cursos de operador de empilhadeira, logística, gestão e gastronomia.
articles.body:
Qualifica SP oferece cursos em seis cidades da Baixada Santista - imagem ilustrativa — Foto: Divulgação/Agência SP

O Qualifica SP está com 505 vagas abertas para cursos presenciais gratuitos de qualificação profissional em seis cidades da Baixada Santista. As oportunidades estão disponíveis em Bertioga , Guarujá , Mongaguá, Peruíbe , Praia Grande e São Vicente ( veja as oportunidades abaixo ).

Em Bertioga, as inscrições terminam neste domingo (25). Nas outras cinco cidades, o prazo vai até 2 de novembro. As inscrições devem ser feitas pelo portal do Governo de São Paulo.

As oportunidades são divididas em três modalidades:

Meu Primeiro Emprego , para pessoas de 16 a 24 anos;

Novo Emprego , para participantes de 25 a 59 anos;

Qualifica SP 60+ , para pessoas com 60 anos ou mais.

Segundo o Governo do Estado, os participantes que terminarem a formação também recebem orientação sobre oportunidades de estágio ou emprego.

articles.title: Associada ACIL, completa 35 anos: a trajetória da ATLAS | G1
articles.standfirst: De Limeira para empresas de diversos setores, a ATLAS une método, tecnologia e atenção pessoal para ajudar empresários a crescer com segurança.
articles.summary: De Limeira para empresas de diversos setores, a ATLAS une método, tecnologia e atenção pessoal para ajudar empresários a crescer com segurança.
articles.body:
Associada ACIL, há 35 anos transformando números em decisões: a trajetória da ATLAS - Crédito: Divulgação.

Em um mercado em que muitos ainda associam contabilidade a guias, prazos e obrigações, a ATLAS construiu sua história com uma proposta diferente: ser parceira estratégica de quem empreende. Há mais de 35 anos no mercado, a empresa atende mais de 300 companhias e atua na área de contabilidade consultiva.

O conceito está resumido na assinatura da marca: Inteligência para Gestão. Na prática, significa entregar ao empresário mais do que relatórios. Significa entregar clareza para decidir.

"Nosso papel é fazer com que o cliente entenda os próprios números e use essa informação a favor do negócio. Gestão profissional, atenção pessoal e resultado real. É isso que nos move", afirma o CEO da ATLAS, Wanderlei Vieira. 0

A trajetória da ATLAS acompanha a evolução do próprio ambiente de negócios. Ao longo das décadas, a empresa ampliofu sua atuação e passou a atender negócios de diferentes portes e segmentos, como indústria, cerâmica, embalagens, alimentos, engenharia, educação e eventos. Hoje, reúne uma equipe de mais de 90 colaboradores.

Um dado que a empresa faz questão de destacar é a longevidade das relações.

"Quem cresce conosco, fica conosco. Muitos clientes estão com a gente há anos, e isso diz muito sobre a confiança que construímos", diz Vieira.

A ATLAS desenvolveu uma metodologia própria de trabalho. A empresa desenvolveu uma metodologia própria, inspirada em boas práticas internacionais de gestão de projetos e adaptada à realidade contábil. O objetivo é contribuir para que cada etapa do processo aconteça de forma mais organizada, com planejamento e clareza.

O processo começa com um onboarding consultivo, em que especialistas conduzem a transição das informações contábeis e fiscais sem perda de histórico. Em seguida, cada cliente passa a contar com um time dedicado, que reúne profissionais de áreas como operação, atendimento, financeiro e sucesso do cliente.

"Método, para nós, não é burocracia. É proteção. Auxilia na organização financeira e na gestão dos processos empresariais.", explica.

Outro pilar da empresa é a integração com os sistemas que os clientes já usam no dia a dia. A equipe da ATLAS é especialista nos principais ERPs do mercado, como Protheus, Omie, Sankhya, Zucchetti e RM, o que permite conectar a contabilidade à operação real de cada negócio.

O atendimento também acompanha as novas formas de trabalhar: a empresa atua com um modelo que combina agilidade digital e proximidade no relacionamento, atendendo clientes de diferentes regiões sem abrir mão do cuidado individual.

Se o método é a estrutura, as pessoas são a inteligência da ATLAS. A empresa mantém uma cultura de melhoria contínua, inspirada no conceito japonês Kaizen, em que os colaboradores são incentivados a propor ideias para aprimorar processos e o atendimento.

"Evoluir todos os dias, juntos. Essa é a nossa cultura. Quando a equipe cresce, o cliente sente a diferença", destaca.

Com a Reforma Tributária em andamento, a ATLAS tem se dedicado a preparar empresários para as mudanças trazidas pela CBS e pelo IBS, com diagnósticos individualizados e capacitações práticas.

"Chegar aos 35 anos é motivo de orgulho, mas o que nos motiva é o próximo passo. Queremos continuar ajudando empresas a crescer com segurança, porque sem dado, não há decisão", conclui.

articles.title: Grupo de dança brasileiro leva samba a bienal de artes folclóricas na Coreia do Sul | G1
articles.standfirst: Com direção de Diego Bernardes, grupo levou um espetáculo sobre o samba e o Carnaval brasileiro à cidade de Jinju e participou de atividades de intercâmbio cultural.
articles.summary: Com direção de Diego Bernardes, grupo levou um espetáculo sobre o samba e o Carnaval brasileiro à cidade de Jinju e participou de atividades de intercâmbio cultural.
articles.body:
O Corpo de Dança Diego Bernardes (CDDB) estreou na cidade de Jinju, na Coreia do Sul — Foto: Divulgação

O Corpo de Dança Diego Bernardes (CDDB) estreou na cidade de Jinju, na Coreia do Sul, onde representa o Brasil na Bienal Mundial de Artes Folclóricas. O grupo apresentou um espetáculo inspirado no samba, no Carnaval brasileiro e nas raízes ancestrais do país.

A direção artística e cênica é de Diego Bernardes, que também atua como diretor artístico e cênico dos Gaviões da Fiel, coreógrafo da Comissão de Frente da X-9 Pioneira de Santos e da Fiel Atibaia.

O elenco de 2027 reúne Aline Andrade, passista dos Gaviões da Fiel; Allysson Serpa, mestre-sala da Amizade da Zona Leste; e Isabelle Gundermann, porta-bandeira dos Gaviões da Fiel.

Além das apresentações, os integrantes participaram de workshops com representantes de outros países, em atividades de intercâmbio cultural e troca de experiências artísticas. Durante a participação na bienal, o grupo também recebeu um reconhecimento.

A presença na programação internacional marca mais uma etapa da trajetória do CDDB, que apresenta elementos do samba e do Carnaval brasileiro ao público de outros países.

articles.title: Motorista morre em batida com ônibus escolar na BR-316, no MA | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente aconteceu na madrugada desta terça-feira (20), em São Luís Gonzaga do Maranhão. Ônibus transportava cerca de 50 estudantes, que não ficaram feridos.
articles.summary: Acidente aconteceu na madrugada desta terça-feira (20), em São Luís Gonzaga do Maranhão. Ônibus transportava cerca de 50 estudantes, que não ficaram feridos.
articles.body:
Motorista morre após colisão frontal entre carro e ônibus com estudantes na BR-316, no Maranhão — Foto: Reprodução/ Divulgação

Um motorista morreu após uma colisão frontal entre um carro de passeio e um ônibus que transportava cerca de 50 estudantes, nesta terça-feira (20), na BR-316, em São Luís Gonzaga do Maranhão . O acidente aconteceu nas proximidades do povoado São Benedito, na entrada do município.

A vítima foi identificada como Renato da Silva Nascimento, que, segundo informações preliminares, tinha mais de 20 anos de experiência como motorista.

De acordo com as primeiras informações, Renato conduzia o carro de passeio quando houve a colisão frontal com o ônibus, que transportava estudantes de uma faculdade de Bacabal com destino à região de Peritoró.

Com a força do impacto, o carro ficou praticamente embaixo do ônibus. Renato não resistiu aos ferimentos e morreu ainda no local do acidente.

O corpo da vítima ficou preso às ferragens, sendo necessária a atuação de uma equipe do Corpo de Bombeiros para realizar o resgate. Apesar da gravidade do acidente, nenhum dos cerca de 50 estudantes que estavam no ônibus ficou ferido, segundo as informações iniciais.

As circunstâncias que provocaram a colisão ainda não foram esclarecidas.

articles.title: IBGE terá seleção com mais de 300 vagas temporárias; o que se sabe | G1
articles.standfirst: Vagas são para profissionais que atuarão em pesquisas sobre emprego, renda e condições de vida da população.
articles.summary: Vagas são para profissionais que atuarão em pesquisas sobre emprego, renda e condições de vida da população.
articles.body:
Agentes Censitários de Pesquisa por Telefone IBGE — Foto: Cal Guimarães/Agência IBGE Notícias

O Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE) recebeu autorização do governo federal para realizar uma nova seleção temporária destinada a atividades de pesquisa por telefone . A medida foi publicada nesta terça-feira (20) no Diário Oficial da União.

Ao todo, estão previstas 325 vagas , sendo 276 para agente de pesquisa por telefone e 49 para supervisor de pesquisa por telefone.

O edital com as regras da seleção deverá ser publicado pelo IBGE em até seis meses, o que significa que o processo poderá ser lançado até abril de 2027.

A autorização consta de uma portaria conjunta dos ministérios da Gestão e da Inovação em Serviços Públicos (MGI) e do Planejamento e Orçamento (MPO).

Os contratados participarão de levantamentos que ajudam a produzir indicadores sobre emprego, renda, atividade econômica e condições de vida da população brasileira.

⚠️ As inscrições ainda não estão abertas. Informações como salários, requisitos de escolaridade, cronograma e etapas da seleção serão divulgadas no edital.

O recrutamento ocorrerá por meio de processo seletivo simplificado , modalidade usada pela administração pública para contratações temporárias.

Por enquanto, não há informações sobre a exigência de escolaridade, o formato das avaliações ou o período de inscrições.

As admissões serão feitas com base na Lei nº 8.745, de 1993, que autoriza a contratação por tempo determinado para atender necessidades temporárias de excepcional interesse público.

A duração dos contratos e possíveis prorrogações seguirá o que determina a legislação. Eventuais extensões deverão ser justificadas pela necessidade de conclusão das atividades de pesquisa.

articles.title: Trump diz que América do Sul está mudando de rumo político | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente dos EUA afirmou nesta segunda-feira (20) que região trocou a esquerda pela direita. Eleições no Brasil não foram citadas.
articles.summary: Presidente dos EUA afirmou nesta segunda-feira (20) que região trocou a esquerda pela direita. Eleições no Brasil não foram citadas.
articles.body:
O presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , afirmou nesta terça-feira (20) que a América do Sul está passando por uma mudança de orientação política, com o avanço da direita. A declaração foi feita no Salão Oval da Casa Branca, durante uma conversa com jornalistas.

Trump foi questionado sobre a possibilidade de apoiar Marine Le Pen na eleição presidencial da França, prevista para o ano que vem. Ele disse que não conhece a política francesa pessoalmente, mas aproveitou a resposta para comentar o cenário sul-americano.

“Se você olhar para o que está acontecendo na América do Sul, as pessoas não acreditariam”, disse Trump. “Estava tudo pendendo muito para a esquerda. Agora está tudo à direita.”

Trump afirmou ainda que todos os candidatos que apoiou na região venceram as eleições. Como exemplo, citou o presidente eleito da Colômbia, a quem elogiou. O Brasil não foi citado.

O presidente dos EUA ainda não declarou apoio formal a nenhum candidato à Presidência do Brasil. Após o primeiro turno, ele afirmou que Flávio Bolsonaro teve uma vitória “apertada, mas impressionante” .

O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, fala com membros da imprensa ao sair da Casa Branca rumo ao Kansas, em Washington, DC, EUA, em 19 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Kevin Lamarque

Na segunda-feira (19), o secretário de Estado americano, Marco Rubio, também comentou o avanço de governos alinhados aos Estados Unidos na América Latina. Em entrevista ao site conservador Breitbart News, ele atribuiu parte dessa mudança à reformulação da política de ajuda externa do governo Trump.

Segundo Rubio, a transferência da gestão de recursos de ajuda estrangeira para o Departamento de Estado e o desmonte da estrutura anterior da Agência dos Estados Unidos para o Desenvolvimento Internacional (USAID) tiveram impacto na região.

O secretário acusou organizações não governamentais latino-americanas de estarem alinhadas à esquerda e serem contrárias aos interesses americanos. Ele também afirmou que os Estados Unidos financiavam muitas delas.

Ele também afirmou que os novos governos não são subordinados aos EUA, mas que compartilham prioridades com Trump, como o combate a organizações ligadas ao narcotráfico e a atração de investimentos americanos.

O Brasil foi citado pelo entrevistador, que mencionou as eleições presidenciais no país. Rubio, no entanto, não comentou o pleito.

articles.title: Igreja de 150 anos, construída com terra compactada, tem licitação aberta para restauro em São José dos Campos | G1
articles.standfirst: Construção da Igreja São Benedito utilizou a taipa de pilão, método tradicional que consiste em compactar terra para formar paredes; edital prevê investimento de R$ 13,7 milhões.
articles.summary: Construção da Igreja São Benedito utilizou a taipa de pilão, método tradicional que consiste em compactar terra para formar paredes; edital prevê investimento de R$ 13,7 milhões.
articles.body:
Igreja São Benedito, no Centro de São José dos Campos, tem cerca de 150 anos de história e deve passar por obras de restauração. — Foto: Bruna Capasciutti/Rede Vanguarda

A Igreja São Benedito, no Centro de São José dos Campos, deve passar por obras de restauração. A Prefeitura abriu uma licitação para contratar os serviços, com investimento estimado em R$ 13,7 milhões.

Com cerca de 150 anos de história, a igreja teve ajuda da população na construção e preserva características arquitetônicas.

Um dos destaques da edificação é a técnica utilizada na construção das paredes: a taipa de pilão, método tradicional que utiliza terra compactada para formar estruturas resistentes.

Por causa dessas características, a restauração deverá respeitar os elementos históricos e construtivos do imóvel, de forma a preservar sua arquitetura original.

As empresas interessadas podem enviar propostas até 14 de dezembro. O prazo para a execução das obras é de até 1 ano e 11 meses.

A Igreja São Benedito é tombada pelo Conselho de Defesa do Patrimônio Histórico, Arqueológico, Artístico e Turístico (Condephaat), órgão estadual responsável pela proteção do patrimônio histórico e cultural.

O imóvel também é protegido pelo conselho municipal responsável pela preservação do patrimônio histórico, arquitetônico, artístico e cultural de São José dos Campos.

Por conta dessa proteção, as intervenções no prédio precisam seguir as regras estabelecidas pelos órgãos responsáveis, garantindo que as características históricas da construção sejam preservadas.

articles.title: Nova etapa retira mais 30 jabutis de praça pública no interior de SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Ao todo, já foram feitas três transferências dos animais que estavam em Adamantina (SP). Segundo a prefeitura, outros 80 jabustis aguardavam novas vagas em unidades especializadas.
articles.summary: Uma nova etapa de transferência retirou mais 30 jabutis-piranga que estavam na Praça Euclides Romanini, em Adamantina (SP). A população chegou a 250 animais.
articles.body:
Nova etapa retira mais 30 jabutis de praça pública onde população chegou a 250 animais em Adamantina (SP) — Foto: Reprodução

Uma nova etapa de transferência retirou mais 30 jabutis-piranga ( Chelonoidis carbonaria ) que estavam na Praça Euclides Romanini, em Adamantina (SP). Eles foram encaminhados para um centro de reabilitação nesta segunda-feira (19).

Ao todo, já foram feitas três transferências dos animais, sendo a mais recente no dia 7 de outubro deste ano, quando outros 50 jabutis haviam sido removidos . A população de jabutis no local chegou a atingir 250 animais.

Nesta segunda-feira, os 30 animais foram encaminhados ao Centro de Triagem e Reabilitação de Animais Silvestres (Cetras) de Registro (SP).

De acordo com a prefeitura, a praça virou abrigo para a espécie após constantes solturas e fugas de animais mantidos irregularmente em cativeiro doméstico por moradores da região.

Ainda permanecem aproximadamente 80 jabutis na praça, que deverão ser transferidos conforme a disponibilização de novas vagas em unidades autorizadas.

Outros 120 jabutis já haviam sido retirados do local e encaminhados ao Centro de Triagem e Reabilitação de Animais Silvestres de São Paulo (Cetras-SP), conforme divulgado pela prefeitura.

A ação foi resultado do trabalho conjunto entre a Prefeitura de Adamantina, o Ministério Público do Estado de São Paulo e o Centro de Triagem e Reabilitação de Animais Silvestres de São Paulo (Cetras-SP).

Novas ações estão sendo planejadas para dar continuidade ao processo de manejo e destinação adequada dos animais, de acordo com o município.

Outros 50 jabutis são transferidos de praça pública de Adamantina (SP) para centro de reabilitação — Foto: Reprodução/Cetra-SP

A Prefeitura de Adamantina também alertou que o abandono, a criação irregular ou a introdução indevida de animais silvestres em áreas urbanas podem configurar infrações e crimes ambientais, sujeitos às penalidades previstas na legislação vigente.

A orientação é para que a população não adquira, abandone ou introduza animais silvestres em espaços públicos e, diante de situações envolvendo fauna silvestre, procure os órgãos competentes para receber a orientação adequada.

Órgãos planejam transferir 180 jabutis de praça de Adamantina (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/Prefeitura

A transferência dos demais animais, segundo as autoridades, exige logística especializada, articulação entre órgãos ambientais de diferentes estados e disponibilidade de instituições habilitadas para recebê-los.

Além disso, o Ministério Público do Estado de São Paulo (MP-SP) informou em 1º de setembro que havia determinado prazos para que as autoridades realocassem os 180 jabutis que viviam em condições inadequadas na praça de Adamantina.

A intervenção do MP-SP ocorre após o espaço público, sem infraestrutura apropriada para a manutenção da espécie, registrar superpopulação e a permanência dos répteis sem previsão de transferência.

Ainda segundo o Ministério Público, não havia um prazo definido para a retirada de todos os animais. A destinação depende, entre outros fatores, de avaliação técnica, disponibilidade de vagas e da existência de instituições regularmente habilitadas para recebê-los.

Em nota, a Secretaria de Meio Ambiente, Infraestrutura e Logística (Semil), por meio da Diretoria de Biodiversidade e Biotecnologia (DBB), informou que a transferência dos demais animais que permanecem no município será realizada de forma gradual, conforme a disponibilidade de vagas na unidade.

Como a espécie não possui ocorrência natural no Estado de São Paulo, os exemplares precisam ser encaminhados para áreas de ocorrência natural após a recuperação. As novas transferências dos animais de Adamantina também estão condicionadas à realização desses processos no Cetras-SP.

articles.title: Parte do teto de escola desaba no Paranoá, no DF, e atinge monitora; veja VÍDEO  | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo relato, alunos estavam no intervalo no momento do desabamento. Monitora foi atingida por parte do material, mas não ficou ferida.
articles.summary: Segundo relato, alunos estavam no intervalo no momento do desabamento. Monitora foi atingida por parte do material, mas não ficou ferida.
articles.body:
Parte do teto da Escola Classe 06 do Paranoá, no Distrito Federal, desabou na tarde desta terça-feira (20).

As imagens (veja o vídeo acima) mostram pedaços do telhado e do forro espalhados sobre mesas e carteiras de uma das salas da escola.

Segundo relato obtido pela TV Globo, o caso aconteceu por volta das 15h, quando os alunos estavam no intervalo. No momento do desabamento, havia uma monitora e um aluno no local.

Um dos pedaços do teto atingiu a monitora, mas ela não ficou ferida. Não há informações sobre outras pessoas atingidas.

Em nota, a Secretaria de Educação do Distrito Federal informou que acompanha o caso e adotou medidas de segurança. A pasta afirma ainda que uma empresa de manutenção predial está no local para avaliar danos e reparos necessários.

Não há informações sobre a causa do desabamento.

Parte de teto de escola desaba no Paranoá, no DF — Foto: Colaborativo/Reprodução

A Secretaria de Estado de Educação do Distrito Federal (SEEDF) informa que a Coordenação Regional de Ensino (CRE) do Paranoá acompanha, desde o primeiro momento, o desabamento de parte do teto de uma sala de aula na Escola Classe 06 do Paranoá.

Imediatamente após o ocorrido, uma equipe da CRE foi à unidade escolar e adotou medidas de segurança, como o isolamento da área e a retirada preventiva dos estudantes das salas próximas. Nenhum estudante ou profissional ficou ferido.

Uma equipe técnica da empresa de manutenção predial está no local para avaliar danos e os reparos necessários. Mudanças no funcionamento das aulas e prazos de conclusão das obras serão definidos após avaliação técnica, priorizando a segurança de todos e a continuidade das atividades pedagógicas.

A SEEDF segue acompanhando o caso para garantir a segurança da comunidade escolar.

articles.summary: Área afetada pela seca no estado passou de 83% para 100% entre agosto e setembro de 2026. Apesar do avanço, intensidade do fenômeno permaneceu estável, segundo o Monitor de Secas.
articles.body:
Seca atinge 100% do território do Maranhão pela primeira vez desde fevereiro, aponta levantamento da ANA — Foto: Divulgação/ANA

A seca atingiu 100% do território do Maranhão em setembro de 2026, segundo dados divulgados nessa segunda-feira (19) pela Agência Nacional de Águas e Saneamento Básico (ANA). O levantamento mostra que a área afetada pelo fenômeno no estado passou de 83%, em agosto, para 100%, em setembro, um aumento de 17 pontos percentuais.

De acordo com o Monitor de Secas, esta é a primeira vez desde fevereiro deste ano que o Maranhão registra seca em toda a sua extensão territorial. Com o resultado, o estado ficou entre os quatro do Nordeste com o maior percentual de área afetada pelo fenômeno, ao lado de Alagoas, Piauí e Sergipe, que também registraram seca em 100% de seus territórios.

Apesar do avanço da área atingida, a intensidade da seca permaneceu estável no Maranhão entre agosto e setembro. Segundo a ANA, pouco mais de 4% do território maranhense apresentou seca moderada, enquanto as demais áreas afetadas registraram condições menos severas.

Ainda assim, o cenário representa a condição mais severa de seca registrada no Maranhão desde fevereiro de 2026.

Nordeste tem maior área afetada pela seca no país

O avanço da seca no Maranhão acompanha o cenário observado em outros estados do Nordeste. Segundo o Monitor de Secas, a região apresentou o maior percentual de área afetada pelo fenômeno no Brasil, chegando a 96% do território em setembro.

Além do Maranhão, outros estados nordestinos registraram aumento da área atingida, como Alagoas, Bahia, Ceará, Paraíba, Pernambuco, Rio Grande do Norte e Sergipe.

Em relação à intensidade, Pernambuco apresentou a situação mais crítica do país em setembro. No estado, a seca grave passou de 28% para 74% do território entre agosto e setembro.

No cenário nacional, a área afetada pela seca aumentou de 67% para 75% do território brasileiro. Enquanto o fenômeno avançou nas regiões Norte e Nordeste, houve redução da área atingida em partes do Centro-Oeste e do Sudeste.

Os três estados da região Sul — Paraná, Santa Catarina e Rio Grande do Sul — permaneceram livres da seca.

Entenda como funciona o Monitor de Secas

O Monitor de Secas é uma ferramenta coordenada pela Agência Nacional de Águas e Saneamento Básico (ANA) que acompanha mensalmente a evolução da seca em todo o Brasil.

O levantamento considera indicadores climáticos e os impactos provocados pela falta de chuvas em diferentes períodos, classificando o fenômeno em cinco categorias de intensidade.

Os dados são utilizados para auxiliar o planejamento e a execução de políticas públicas de enfrentamento à seca.

O monitoramento é realizado nos 26 estados e no Distrito Federal, permitindo acompanhar a evolução da área afetada e da intensidade do fenômeno ao longo dos meses.

Os resultados podem ser consultados no site oficial do Monitor de Secas .

articles.body:
Escola Municipal Nerone Maiolino em Campo Grande — Foto: Prefeitura

O segundo turno das Eleições 2026, marcado para domingo (25), vai provocar alterações nas aulas de 176 unidades de ensino de Campo Grande e Nioaque, entre escolas municipais, estaduais, Escolas Municipais de Educação Infantil (Emeis) e Centros de Educação Infantil (Ceinfs).

A Secretaria Municipal de Educação (Semed) informou ao g1 que as unidades que funcionarão como locais de votação terão as aulas suspensas na tarde de sexta-feira (23) e na manhã de segunda-feira (26).

Segundo a secretaria, a suspensão é necessária para a organização das salas que receberão os eleitores, além da limpeza e reorganização dos espaços após a votação.

A Semed destacou ainda que, até o momento, não recebeu comunicação oficial sobre possíveis alterações nas seções eleitorais para o segundo turno.

articles.title: Sir Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr back new Beatles attraction
articles.summary: The surviving Beatles have welcomed plans for an immersive visitor experience in Liverpool.
articles.body:
Sir Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr have backed plans for a major new Beatles visitor attraction in Liverpool.

The development will see The Beatles Story move from Albert Dock to the former St John's Market site, alongside a new Yellow Submarine experience at St John's Beacon.

McCartney said he "can't wait" for people to be able to "step into our story", while Starr said: "Liverpool was, and still is, Music City".

The attraction will feature immersive technology, original artefacts and recreated sets charting the band's rise from post-war Liverpool to international fame.

Apple Corps Ltd, which manages The Beatles' creative and business interests, will take over operation of The Beatles Story in 2027 ahead of its relocation the following year.

The attraction has been based at Albert Dock since 1990. Under the plans, it would move to the former St John's Market Hall, vacant since the market closed in 2024. At 100,000 sq ft, the new site would be more than four times the size of the current attraction, while the former Radio City tower, St John's Beacon , would house a new Yellow Submarine experience.

It follows plans unveiled earlier this year for an official Beatles attraction at 3 Savile Row in London , where the band staged their final public performance during a famous rooftop concert in 1969. Fans will be able to explore seven floors of memorabilia and archive material connected to the band when it opens in 2027.

Announcing the Liverpool plans, Apple Corps chief executive Tom Greene said Liverpool was getting a Beatles destination worthy of the city's musical heritage.

"Just like Graceland or Dollywood, it's fitting that The Beatles will have a world-class destination for fans to visit in the city where the story started," he said.

Apple Corps said visitors would be taken on a journey from the band's post-war Liverpool roots through Hamburg, The Cavern, Beatlemania, Abbey Road, Shea Stadium, Savile Row and beyond.

Commenting on the announcement Sir Paul McCartney said: "I love Liverpool. It's part of who I am, it's part of who The Beatles are.

"I find it incredible and humbling that people are still interested in our story and it's very exciting to me that The Beatles Story and The Beacon are being transformed in such an exciting way in the heart of Liverpool city.

"It couldn't have happened without Liverpool and I can't wait for people to be able to step into our story and share the experience."

Tickets sold for The Beatles Story will contribute to the The Apple Corps Liverpool Trust, a charitable initiative to provide support and opportunities for emerging local artists.

Ringo Starr said: "Liverpool was, and still is, Music City.

"And now we are expanding The Beatles Story Experience in Liverpool - how far out. The beat goes on.

"I also love that proceeds from every ticket will go back to support new Liverpool artists. It is great to be part of this. Deep down I am still a scouser. I love what Apple Corps and Liverpool are doing."

The project is a partnership between Apple Corps, Liverpool City Council and Liverpool City Region Combined Authority, with support from central government.

Liverpool City Region Mayor Steve Rotheram said it felt right that the "definitive Beatles experience" should be located in the city where the band's story began.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: "The Beatles are one of the greatest examples of what Britain can give to the world.

"Four young men from Liverpool changed music and popular culture forever and, more than 60 years later, their story is still a source of enormous pride for this city and for our whole country."

Reflecting on what his bandmates would have made of the plans, Sir Paul McCartney said: "If you'd told us this was going to happen when we were hanging out and getting started, we'd never have believed it."

articles.title: Guernsey's Specsavers founders get lifetime retail award
articles.summary: Douglas and Dame Mary Perkins started the company in their spare bedroom in 1984.
articles.body:
Specsavers' founders have been given a lifetime award for their role in "transforming access to optical and audiology care".

The multinational company was started in Guernsey by Douglas and Dame Mary Perkins on a table-tennis table in their spare bedroom in 1984. The company now has more than 2,600 stores in 11 countries.

They were recognised with the Lifetime Contribution Award, at the Retail Gazette Awards last week, which seeks to honour people shape the future of the industry.

Dame Mary said she was "genuinely surprised" to receive the award, and described it as a "real honour to be recognised".

She said: "It's a real honour to be recognised by the industry, especially as Doug and I approach 60 years in optics.

"What makes it even more special is knowing that Specsavers has only ever been possible because of the passion and commitment of our partners and colleagues.

"They've helped shape the business from day one and continue to make a difference for our customers every day."

Stressing that the benefits of economic cooperation must reach all sections of society, he reaffirmed India’s support for the adoption of an action plan for the multilateral trade and economic cooperation programme for the period 2026-2030.The minister stressed that connectivity must be based on consultation and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all countries, adding that projects not founded on these principles will not be sustainable. articles.title: Shinde calls INDIA bloc ‘ten-headed Ravana’, accuses Uddhav of ‘vote theft’
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde on Tuesday accused Uddhav Thackeray of stealing the people's mandate after the 2019 assembly
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde on Tuesday accused Uddhav Thackeray of stealing the people's mandate after the 2019 assembly elections and called the INDIA bloc a “ten-mouthed Ravana” whose effigy should be burnt. Addressing his party's Dussehra rally in Mumbai, Shinde attacked the opposition over its allegations of vote theft, accused it of undermining constitutional institutions and said the government would support farmers facing crop losses due to water scarcity.Without naming Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray, Shinde alleged that the actual “vote theft” took place after the 2019 Maharashtra assembly elections, when the undivided Shiv Sena joined hands with the NCP and Congress to form a government.“You did not even contest the election. You made a backdoor entry and became chief minister. You stabbed the mandate and grabbed the post. It was a huge dacoity against the people's mandate,” he said.Shinde questioned the opposition's allegations of irregularities in electoral rolls, saying it had earlier raised concerns over an increase in voter numbers and was now questioning the deletion of names.“This is double standards and a daily show of new drama. The INDIA bloc is a ten-mouthed Ravana, and we need to burn its effigy,” he said, accusing the opposition of seeking to undermine the Constitution drafted by Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar.He also questioned why the opposition had not alleged vote theft when the INDIA bloc won elections in Telangana, Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh. “When you lose, you call it vote chori and start alleging foul play. The INDIA bloc won elections in Telangana, Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh. Why was there no vote chori then?” he asked.Shinde accused the Congress of looting the country for 70 years and alleged that it was now demanding ballot papers after previously winning elections through booth capturing.He also hit out at opposition leaders for their remarks on regime changes in Bangladesh, Nepal and Sri Lanka, accusing them of encouraging anarchy in India.“This is Hindustan, a new India. This is an India that enters Pakistan,” he said, adding that people would teach a lesson to those he described as anti-national.Questioning the opposition's criticism of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah, Shinde said Modi had made India the world's fourth-largest economy and received the highest civilian awards from 36 countries. He also claimed there was no corruption case against the prime minister.“Why use such foul and low language against our PM?” he asked.Shinde further accused opposition leaders of speaking in Pakistan's favour and alleged that their statements were being used to create headlines there. Referring to Captain Smit Machchhar, who saved a plane during an attack, he said the pilot had acknowledged drawing inspiration from Modi.Shinde claimed that Modi, the US president and the Israeli prime minister had congratulated the pilot, while some opposition leaders had not.“Whatever they say here becomes a headline in Pakistan. This is a huge conspiracy...Why do you speak in favour of Pakistan? This is unfortunate. This is sedition and not any kind of love for India,” he alleged.The deputy chief minister also criticised Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for organising a rally against the Supreme Court, alleging that it amounted to an insult to the judiciary and an attack on a constitutional institution.“On the one hand, they hold the Constitution in their hands, and on the other, their actions amount to an attack on it. They are moving towards dividing the country,” he said.Taking a swipe at the opposition's demand for the election of the chief election commissioner, Shinde sarcastically asked whether it would also seek elections for the chief justice of India and municipal corporation chiefs.He alleged that opposition parties were promoting a “fake narrative” of vote theft through rallies in Mumbai while farmers were struggling with crop losses.Turning to the agrarian crisis, Shinde said Maharashtra was facing drought-like conditions as standing crops dried up due to a weak monsoon. He announced that he had dispatched an initial 100 tonnes of foodgrains to distressed farmers as an advance Diwali gift, with more consignments to follow.“Today, I have dispatched the first tranche of 100 tonnes of foodgrains to farmers as an advance Diwali gift. There will be more such rounds of assistance given to farmers,” he said.Shinde said excessive rainfall had washed away land last year, causing serious losses to crops and cattle. This year, the monsoon had failed to provide adequate relief to farmers, he added.“Unfortunately, this year, the monsoon turned its back on farmers. We reached out to distressed farmers who are shedding tears and offered them consolation. This is not the time to politicise the farmers' plight but to extend support to them,” he said.Describing himself as a farmer's son, Shinde said he understood the hardships faced by cultivators and their families. articles.title: CDC reports third measles death in the United States this year
articles.summary: The death was added to the federal tally, as the US records more than 4,400 measles cases nationwide.
articles.body:
The Centers for Disease Control (CDC) has reported that a third person has died due to measles in the United States, as the country grapples with its largest measles outbreak in decades.

The CDC did not specify on Tuesday in which state the death occurred. The agency’s national tally remains lower than the number of measles-related deaths reported by state officials, particularly in Pennsylvania , the state hardest hit by the outbreak. Pennsylvania had reported 1,286 cases and five deaths as of Monday.

The CDC confirmed a death on Tuesday after the National Center for Health Statistics verified that measles was listed as the underlying cause of death on a death certificate.

The CDC reported 4,410 measles cases nationwide as of October 15. The agency has said its death count could change as further reviews are completed. The outbreak in Pennsylvania has spread well beyond its initial epicentre in Lancaster County, with 42 counties now reporting cases.

The federal government’s approach to counting measles deaths has drawn scrutiny after the CDC shifted to relying on mortality data from the National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS) rather than state health departments’ reports.

The CDC has previously told Al Jazeera that it is working with the Council of State and Territorial Epidemiologists to establish a standardised definition for measles deaths. In the meantime, they will use NCHS mortality data as their measure.

articles.title: Farage promises to scrap tax on pay for armed forces reservists
articles.summary: A large group of protesters turned up outside the Reform UK rally in Plymouth with Nigel Farage.
articles.body:
The leader of Reform UK, Nigel Farage, has told a rally in Plymouth he would get rid of tax on pay for armed forces reservists.

Farage said he wanted to get more people in the reserves at the event for party supporters as part of Reform's 100 Days to Save Britain tour.

When questioned by the BBC over a Reform councillor in Plymouth who was investigated and cleared over social media posts, Farage said he was "still part of the party was because everyone believes he's a solid bloke".

About 100 protesters against Reform gathered outside the Plymouth Arena near the city centre, chanting before, during and after the event.

Farage spoke to about 300 Reform members and councillors and opened his speech by paying tribute to Ann Widdecombe, who was killed at her home in Devon .

On cutting tax for reservists, he said: "Anyone that signs up as a reservist and does their bit will face no tax on the pay they receive.

"Let's get more men and women signing up for the reserves."

When asked by the BBC about the UK deploying fighter jets to defend Saudi Arabia , Farage said the UK was "not even a player any more".

He said: "Should we help with peacekeeping missions? As much as we can.

"But what we've got to face up to is the reality that we've lost our ability to be an effective player".

Plymouth Reform councillor Ben Rowe was investigated in May after being accused of sharing Islamophobic posts on social media but was then cleared.

The BBC asked Farage if Rowe's behaviour had been acceptable.

He said: "These are working class people, going into politics, venting their spleen on certain issues and maybe there's a little bit of political growing up to do.

"But let's not condemn everybody for everything they say, and the reason he's still part of the party is because everyone believes he's a solid bloke."

Outside the event, amid a significant police presence, protesters gathered with placards and joined in chants saying Farage was not welcome in the city.

Liam Condron-Farnos, from the campaign group Stand Up To Racism, said: "The way he's built his politics over the years, and still is, is on anti-immigrant hysteria.

"We need to show him that's not an uncontested view in this country."

articles.title: In 2008-09, a Wisconsin county tested leftover cheese brine on roads; the unusual mix reduced salt use by 30-40% and remained liquid after two days at −21°F
articles.summary: Discover how Wisconsin has revolutionized winter road maintenance by utilizing cheese brine, cutting salt usage significantly while remaining effective in extreme cold. Learn about the benefits and challenges of this innovative solution.
articles.body: Wisconsin is one of the biggest cheese-producing states in the country, and it also has long, hard winters that keep highway crews working through the night. Wisconsin’s dairies and its highway departments seem to have little in common, but both handle large amounts of salt. Some of the brined cheeses, like mozzarella or provolone, are treated with brine or salty liquid. The brine has to be disposed of, which costs the dairy money. Road crews spread salt on roads, but a significant portion does not stay in place. Instead, it can bounce off the pavement or be scattered by passing traffic. To address this problem, one rural county decided to try an unconventional solution.Emil Norby’s brine trial in Polk CountyEmil “Moe” Norby of the Polk County Highway Department started the project in 2008, inspired by the fact that dairies soak cheese in brine, as ForConstructionPros reported. The brine came from F & A Dairy Products in Dresser, Wisconsin, which turns out thousands of gallons of it each year. The brine is filtered before the county picks it up. Norby conducted a study on test roads during the 2008 to 2009 winter. NPR reported that, depending on the amount of material applied, the study found salt savings of 30 to 40%. Minnesota Public Radio reported that the 2008-09 findings led the county to use the brine more widely, and NPR noted in January 2014 that the county had put down 38,000 gallons of it the winter before.The point, Norby later said, was to see whether a waste stream from cheesemaking could do the same job for less money. Minnesota Public Radio reported that the test roads let Norby compare ordinary salt with the cheese-brine mix under real winter conditions, and that the brine helped the salt stick to the pavement instead of bouncing off. Norby also reported better results at colder temperatures, which let the county use less salt and stretch its supply.A field test and the −6°F freezing limit of salt brineAccording to the Federal Highway Administration, the eutectic composition of a sodium chloride brine is about 23% salt by weight, and a brine at that concentration freezes at about −6°F (−21°C). Norby left 12 ounces of the brine outside and found that it did not freeze until after two consecutive days at −21°F, a result colder than the −6°F limit for sodium chloride brine, so it is best read as an informal observation.The brine’s main function is pre-wetting, which coats the rock salt before it is spread. Emil Norby told The New York Times that dry road salt can lose about 30% of its material to bounce and traffic, a figure consistent with a Michigan Department of Transportation study that found roughly 30% of dry salt is lost to bounce and scatter. The same study reported that pre-wetting salt with brine significantly reduces those losses.What the brine cost compared with magnesium chlorideMagnesium chloride would cost $1.29 a gallon, ForConstructionPros reported, while hauling the brine himself would cost just 9 cents a gallon, saving the county $40,000 in its first year. Sources differ on what the $40,000 figure represents: ForConstructionPros ties it to replacing magnesium chloride, while The New York Times, as relayed by Sustainable Brands, describes it as $40,000 saved on rock salt, so it is best read as one reported saving whose basis is unclear. The dairy made some profit as well. Chuck Engdahl, wastewater manager at F & A Dairy Products, said the company saves roughly $20,000 per year by giving excess cheese brine to road crews instead of paying to haul it away for disposal.Milwaukee’s 2013 pilot and the limits of the ideaIt was said that Milwaukee was the largest city to test the cheese brine for road deicing, and Modern Farmer reported that if the test succeeded, it would be the largest city to use the solution. Farm and Dairy, citing the Times, mentions that the city used 44,000 tons of salt in 2012, which cost the city $6.5 million in terms of dealing with snow and ice. At the same time, it was estimated that the pilot would cost only around $6,500. The Times further reports that the pilot involved only eight gallons of brine per ton of rock salt, and the Associated Press also mentions that the city was going to find a provider of mozzarella or provolone brine.This method has its disadvantages. Norby described the brine’s smell as mild, and Milwaukee’s Department of Public Works describes it as having “a distinctive odor.” HuffPost also highlights that the brine will not substitute for salt because it serves as a primer so that roads require less of it. Nonetheless, cheese brine still deposits sodium chloride, and consequently chloride, into the environment. The advantage is only the lesser quantity of salt.Why less salt matters for lakes: the 2017 findingsChloride does not disappear after the snow melts. The Cary Institute reports that the 2017 study Salting our freshwater lakesfound long-term salinization in 44% of sampled lakes in the Midwest and Northeast; impervious land cover was the key predictor, and even 1% development around a lake increased the odds of long-term salinization. Cheese brine still deposits sodium chloride, so its benefit is applying less salt overall.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: Russia's defence ministry on Tuesday said its forces had struck five cargo vessels in Ukraine and two logistics hubs, alleging that the targets were being used for military purposes.The Russian military struck three cargo vessels in Ukraine's port of Reni and two others en route to Odesa, the ministry said, according to Reuters. Russian forces also hit two logistics hubs, one in the Volyn region and another in the city of Khmelnytskyi, it added, as per Reuters.The claims come amid intensified Russian attacks on Ukraine, which has been facing shortages of US-made Patriot air defence systems and PAC-3 interceptors capable of intercepting Russian ballistic missiles.The shortage has added to concerns over Kyiv's ability to defend itself against incoming attacks, with air raid alerts increasingly becoming part of daily life as civilians seek shelter.US secretary of state Marco Rubio on Tuesday said Washington had not deliberately withheld missile interceptors from Ukraine, explaining that several countries were seeking the weapons and that the US had to maintain sufficient supplies for its own global defence commitments.Rubio said missile interceptors were currently among the most sought-after products in the defence sector, with the US required to meet minimum operational requirements across its military installations and air defence networks worldwide.“When a country doesn't get interceptors from the United States, it's not because we're denying. We have our own. We have minimum standards that we have to meet internally in our base presence all over the world,” he said.Emphasising that Washington had not intentionally denied Ukraine access to the weapons, Rubio said US forces also had to account for defence requirements at installations around the world.“We have a global defence footprint, and many of our installations around the world are part of defence, air defence. So there's nothing being deliberately denied to Ukraine,” he added.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Meet Gregor Corse, 5-year-old with neurological condition raises $100,000 for charity by walking 30 laps daily for 30 days, wins Pride of Britain award, now wants to plan another fundraiser to help others
articles.summary: A five-year-old boy from Scotland has won hearts with his determination to help others, raising more than $100,000 for charity by walking laps around his
articles.body: A five-year-old boy from Scotland has won hearts with his determination to help others, raising more than $100,000 for charity by walking laps around his house. Gregor Corse, from the Orkney Islands, took on the challenge despite living with an undiagnosed neurological condition that affects his balance and motor skills. His inspiring efforts have earned him the title of Youngest Fundraiser of the Year at the 2026 Pride of Britain Awards.According to PEOPLE, Gregor was born with the condition and took longer than expected to reach developmental milestones. His mother, Iona, recalled that he began crawling at around two and a half years old and took his first steps at almost four.How Stephen Hendry inspired Gregor Corse to walkGregor’s journey towards independent walking began with an unexpected source of inspiration: British snooker player Stephen Hendry.His mother told PEOPLE that Gregor had been watching Hendry on YouTube when he expressed a desire to walk around his own pool table.“Gregor has a little pool table,” Iona explained. “I was sitting in front of the TV when he said, ‘Mommy, I’d love to be able to walk around the table like Stephen Hendry.’”Iona helped him walk around the table using his pool cue as a walking stick. Soon, Gregor let go and continued walking on his own.To encourage him further, she created a reward chart featuring small pool balls she had painted and arranged in a triangle. Each time Gregor walked from one room to another, he could choose a ball and place it on the chart.“That really motivated him,” she said.Although Gregor gradually began walking independently at home, he continued to use a walking frame outdoors. Eventually, he told his mother that he wanted to walk outside like other children.Gregor takes on a 30-day walking challenge for charityDetermined to help her son achieve his goal, Iona supported Gregor as he decided to walk 30 laps around their house every day for 30 days.He initially wanted to complete 50 laps daily, but his mother felt it was important to set a manageable target.“He originally thought he could do 50, but I didn’t want to make it too difficult,” she said.The mother-son duo decided to raise money for Inclusive Orkney, a local charity that supports children with additional needs.Iona admitted that she initially hesitated before launching the fundraising campaign on JustGiving.“I was about to publish the JustGiving page when I wondered if it was silly to ask people to donate,” she recalled. “I nearly closed it, but then I thought that even a couple of hundred pounds would be better than nothing.”What began as a personal challenge soon grew into a community-wide effort.Local businesses, police and firefighters rally behind GregorGregor wore a kilt on the first day of his walking challenge. When he wore a jacket displaying a local business’s logo the following day, Iona saw an opportunity to involve more businesses in the initiative.“I asked Gregor to name the local businesses that meant something to him, and we made a list,” she said. “Fueled by adrenaline, I messaged them to ask if they’d sponsor a day. Everyone was delighted to do it.”As news of Gregor’s efforts spread, neighbours began asking if they could join him. Local media covered his journey, while police officers and firefighters also turned up to show their support.“It became an event for Gregor, not just a walking challenge,” Iona told PEOPLE.Gregor said the challenge made him feel stronger. He particularly enjoyed seeing a fire engine and a lorry arrive to support him.Reflecting on the response from the community, Iona described the experience as deeply moving.“There was so much support, and people gave Gregor gifts,” she said. “He’d never had anything like that before. ‘Heartwarming’ is probably the best word.”Gregor Corse raises more than $100,000 for Inclusive OrkneyGregor’s walking challenge has raised more than £80,000, equivalent to approximately $106,000, for Inclusive Orkney.His fundraising achievement also earned him recognition at the 2026 Pride of Britain Awards, where he was named Youngest Fundraiser of the Year.Iona recalled bursting into tears when she received the news that her son had won the award. The call came shortly after she dropped him off at preschool, on the 19th anniversary of her grandmother’s death.“I was thinking how much I wished she could see Gregor and how proud she’d be,” she said.Iona admitted that she never expected Gregor to receive the honour, particularly given the number of children recognised for their extraordinary efforts.“I never expected it. To me, he’s the most phenomenal boy in the world, but there are so many other children doing amazing things that you hear about on Pride of Britain,” she explained. “I never, in my wildest dreams, thought he’d win.”What’s next for Gregor?Despite the scale of his achievement, Gregor may not be finished with fundraising. According to Iona, he has already asked whether he can take on another challenge to help people.“For a child of 4 or 5 to say he wants to do another fundraiser to help people, I think that shows how much this has done for his mindset,” she said.While Iona is unsure whether Gregor fully understands the significance of his award, he is excited about attending the ceremony at the Grosvenor House Hotel in London on Monday, October 19.For now, the young fundraiser has a simple message for everyone who supported his efforts.“Thank you,” Gregor said.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2024, a New Jersey dissertation reported on asphalt that heats itself; conductive road strips maintained a snow-free surface at about 6 watts per square foot
articles.summary: New Jersey researchers develop self-heating asphalt that maintains snow-free roads using low energy consumption. Conductive road strips tested at Rowan University showcase significant potential for winter maintenance and safety. Discover innovative solutions in asphalt technology for cold weather conditions.
articles.body: Clearing snow from pavement usually means either removing it by force or dissolving it with chemicals. Plows scrape the road surface, while salt changes how water freezes and then drains into soil and water systems. Both methods require labor, equipment and repeated passes through a storm. A third method uses the road itself as the heating element. Because asphalt is not a good conductor of electricity, engineers must add conductive materials and electrodes to the asphalt layers to heat it with current. The current warms the asphalt enough to melt snow, and the technology has been tested at Rowan University’s accelerated pavement testing facility in southern New Jersey.The CREATES test strips in GlassboroThe research comes from the Center for Research and Education in Advanced Transportation Engineering Systems (CREATES), part of Rowan University’s Henry M. Rowan College of Engineering. The center is housed at the South Jersey Technology Park on Rowan University’s West Campus in New Jersey. The team worked with the U.S. Army Engineer Research and Development Center’s Cold Regions Research and Engineering Laboratory. ASME reports that the conductive mixture contains 30% graphite and 1% carbon fiber by volume of asphalt binder. In a study published in Transportation Research Record, researchers from Rowan University reported that their laboratory-prepared conductive asphalt mixtures achieved an electrical resistivity of 1 to 2 ohm-meters (Ω·m), averaging 1.21 Ω·m.The first one was the control strip without any electrodes. The second design used a 0.4-inch conductive layer with steel electrodes spaced 6 and 12 inches apart. The third used a 1-inch conductive layer with electrodes spaced 12 inches apart in one section and 6 inches apart in the other. The New Jersey field tests were conducted during the winters of 2021 and 2022, according to Rowan University’s announcement.What the Transportation Research Record paper found about powerRowan announced the full-scale results in November 2023, after the paper appeared in Transportation Research Record that year. The paper, Full-Scale Evaluation of Electrically Conductive Asphalt Pavements for Deicing Applications, covered the winters of 2021 and 2022. Rowan University announced the full-scale test results on November 29, 2023. The research paper appeared in Transportation Research Record, volume 2679, issue 1, in January 2025. The paper says the team built three 30-by-15-foot full-scale strips at Rowan University’s Accelerated Pavement Testing Facility: one control lane and two electrically conductive sections.Strip II used an asphalt binder with conductive fibers, while strip III used a modified high-performance thin overlay with graphite and carbon fibers; strip III also let the researchers compare 12-inch and 6-inch electrode spacing under the same 24V AC setup. ASME reported that strip two consumed about three times more power than strip three, but the paper’s abstract gives 19.75 watts per square foot for strip two against 4.92 for strip three, which is nearly four times as much.The 6 watts per square foot figure in Marath’s 2024 dissertationThe lowest-power result appears in a doctoral dissertation by Ashith Marath, Development of Electrically Conductive Asphalt Pavements for Deicing Applications in Cold Regions, approved at Rowan on September 26, 2024. The abstract of the dissertation says the conductive asphalt test strips could maintain a snow-free pavement surface with a thermal power output as low as 6 watts per square foot (65 watts per square meter) under winter conditions in New Jersey. The abstract of Marath’s laboratory study says mixtures with 30% graphite had electrical resistivity similar to those with 15% graphite and 2% carbon fiber. Accelerated truck loading using a Heavy Vehicle Simulator found that the heated strips worked about as well as regular asphalt.Operating costs of $2,280 per hour and the airfield use casePower demand determines the running cost, so the low-power finding matters here. ASME’s estimate of $2,280 an hour for a million square feet at $0.19 per kilowatt-hour works out to about 12 watts per square foot, which is double the dissertation’s 6 watts and well above the 4.92 watts per square foot reported for the third strip, so the figures are not directly comparable. Heating cannot fully offset the cost of manual snow and ice removal, which is why Yusuf Mehta, the center’s director, said the system is designed mainly for short stretches such as airports and bridges, where safety and uninterrupted operation justify the expense. The system was also being tested in Alaska during fall 2023 and winter 2024. Life expectancy becomes another reason to use heated pavements. Plows set at the wrong height can damage the asphalt and peel off the sealant, while deicing salts accelerate freeze-thaw damage and shorten the pavement’s life.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Beverly Hills mansion once owned by Warner Bros. co-founder Harry Warner was restored with its Old Hollywood details intact; first listed for nearly $40 million in 2016, it finally sold for $27.25 million
articles.summary: A Beverly Hills mansion once owned by Warner Bros.
articles.body: A Beverly Hills mansion once owned by Warner Bros. co-founder Harry Warner has sold for $27.25 million, nearly a decade after it first hit the market for $39.99 million. The historic property, restored by former owner Daphna Ziman to retain its Old Hollywood character, had been listed on and off for years before the deal was reported by The Wall Street Journal. The 1923-built estate features hand-carved oak, leaded-glass windows, a screening room with silk velvet curtains and a guesthouse associated with Marilyn Monroe. Its sale price was below its original asking price of nearly $40 million and its most recent reported asking price of $31.5 million.A mansion with a Hollywood legacyLocated at 1005 North Woodland Drive in Beverly Hills, California, the estate was built in 1923 for Harry Warner, one of the four brothers who established Warner Bros. Studios. According to Realtor.com, Warner commissioned architect Paul R. Williams to design the residence, combining French Country influences with Tudor-style elements.Williams was a pioneering architect who became the first African American member of the American Institute of Architects. His work helped shape the appearance of several prominent Los Angeles homes, and the Warner mansion reflects the period's preference for elaborate detailing, generous entertaining spaces and a mix of European architectural influences.The property is spread across approximately 1.1 acres, with the main residence measuring around 12,000 square feet. Reports have described it as a seven-bedroom mansion, although published accounts differ on the exact number of bathrooms and the total square footage. The estate also includes a guesthouse, a swimming pool, a tennis court and landscaped gardens.Harry Warner reportedly owned the house during the 1940s. Its guesthouse has been associated with Marilyn Monroe, who is said to have stayed there while Warner occupied the main residence. This detail has appeared in real-estate coverage, including the original 2016 listing reports.Preserving its Old Hollywood characterThe mansion's more recent history is closely tied to Ziman, a filmmaker, philanthropist and founder of the cable television network Cinémoi. She and her then-husband, real-estate investor Richard Ziman, purchased the property in 1996.Rather than strip the house of its traditional character, the owners undertook an extensive renovation that sought to restore its historic atmosphere while incorporating modern amenities. According to a 2016 Los Angeles Times report, the renovation took more than three years to bring the house back to its former glory.The work involved removing later finishes and restoring architectural details. Ziman told the newspaper that photographs helped her recreate the house's earlier appearance. Hand-painted kitchen tiles were reproduced, while the renovation exposed wooden beams and other details that had been concealed by false ceilings.The property also incorporates some period-inspired elements sourced from elsewhere. According to the Los Angeles Times, these included leaded-glass windows acquired in Italy, wooden beams from a church in England and a 16th-century fireplace purchased at auction from the Palace of Versailles. The distinction matters: the restoration preserved and revived historic features, but not every decorative element was necessarily original to the house.The result was a residence designed to retain its Old Hollywood atmosphere rather than resemble a newly built contemporary mansion. Listing agent Joyce Rey's website highlighted the hand-carved oak, leaded-glass windows, hand-painted kitchen tiles and silk velvet curtains in the screening room as defining features of the restored property.A home built for entertainingThe estate was also used as a venue for political and philanthropic gatherings. Ziman hosted fundraisers and events attended by prominent political figures, and the Los Angeles Times reported in 2016 that more than 80,000 guests had visited the property over the years.Its entertainment spaces include a screening room, a library, a game room and a lounge with an indoor-outdoor bar. The screening room's silk velvet curtains reportedly came from a downtown Los Angeles theatre, adding another layer of cinematic history to the house.The grounds feature a European-style garden, a rock-lagoon-like pool and spa, waterfalls, a tennis court and a koi pond crossed by a footbridge. The guesthouse and extensive entertaining areas helped make the property suitable for both private gatherings and large events.The mansion also had a television appearance of its own. It was used as O.J. Simpson's home in the 2016 FX series The People v. O.J. Simpson: American Crime Story. Several rooms and the garden appeared in the production, bringing renewed attention to the property when it was first listed for nearly $40 million that year.A long road to the final saleThe mansion's journey to a buyer was not straightforward. It first appeared on the market in August 2016 for $40 million, according to The Real Deal. The asking price subsequently changed, and the property went on and off the market over the following years.In March 2022, The Real Deal reported that the estate was under contract with a last asking price of $32.5 million. That report did not establish a completed sale, and the property later returned to the market. By the time of the final transaction reported by The Wall Street Journal, the asking price had reportedly been reduced to $31.5 million.The reported $27.25 million sale represents a substantial reduction from the original asking price, although the two figures reflect different stages of a long marketing process rather than a simple price cut at one time. The buyer's identity was not disclosed in the Wall Street Journal report.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: In 2026, a deep-sea robot filmed a black swallower off Trinidad and Tobago with a distended belly after it gulped prey up to 10 times its weight
articles.summary: Explore how a black swallower, a deep-sea predator, captured on film by SuBastian, swallowed prey ten times its weight during a groundbreaking marine expedition by the Schmidt Ocean Institute.
articles.body: The deep ocean is home to animals with unusual ways of finding and consuming food. Some predators have evolved to swallow prey much larger than themselves, an adaptation that can be especially useful where meals are difficult to find. During a deep-sea expedition off Trinidad and Tobago in 2026, researchers captured footage of a black swallower with a remarkably distended stomach after consuming a large meal. The encounter involved the black swallower (Chiasmodon niger), a deep-sea fish known for swallowing prey far larger than itself. The video recording was made as part of a survey led by Trinidadian marine biologist Diva Amon.ROV SuBastian filmed the black swallower during the June 29 to July 28, 2026 expeditionThe sighting took place during the Schmidt Ocean Institute’s Deep Wonders of Trinidad and Tobago expedition, which ran from June 29 to July 28, 2026, as the institute’s cruise page lists. The month-long survey was conducted aboard the research vessel Falkor (too), with researchers using the remotely operated vehicle SuBastian to explore underwater habitats. The Schmidt Ocean Institute describes the expedition as the first locally led and most comprehensive deep-sea survey of Trinidad and Tobago’s surrounding waters, and its announcement confirms that the team captured footage of a black swallower with a distended stomach after it had eaten a meal much larger than itself.The fish can swallow prey up to ten times its own weightThe black swallower is a small deep-sea predator with an unusual feeding strategy. Its large mouth, elongated lower jaw and expandable stomach allow it to engulf fish much larger than itself. The Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution’s black swallower profile explains that the species can swallow prey weighing up to ten times its own mass. Its backward-pointing, interlocking teeth help hold prey in place and prevent it from escaping once swallowed. This feeding behavior is especially advantageous in the deep sea, where food may be scarce and finding food sources might be random. Eating much in a single hunt gives the fish much energy without having to hunt for food continuously.Its distended stomach revealed an unusual adaptationWhat stood out in the video was the extreme swelling of the fish’s abdomen. The fish’s stomach had swollen to hold a meal much larger than it could normally carry. The black swallower was one of many observations made during the survey. The team documented 25 cold seeps and the institute’s announcement says the mapping covered about 13% of Trinidad and Tobago’s marine territory.Cold seeps are areas where there is emission of methane and other substances from the seabed, providing a habitat for organisms that have adapted to the chemically rich environment. Such records helped scientists establish the distribution of deep-sea organisms and pinpoint areas that might require further investigation. The project showed the value of local scientists using ROVs, seafloor mapping and specimen collection in marine research.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: About 65 million years ago, after dinosaurs died, a giant fungus may have risen as forests filled with dead plants left behind by the mass extinction
articles.summary: Research reveals a significant increase in fungal activity following the mass extinction 65 million years ago, suggesting fungi played a vital role in ecosystem recovery.
articles.body: When a mass extinction transforms an ecosystem, the organisms that survive can find themselves in a very different world. The asteroid impact at the end of the Cretaceous Period disrupted ecosystems and left large amounts of dead organic material. Following the event, fungi could have thrived in environments where there was an abundance of food.Fossil remains reveal a fungal bloom after the asteroid impactIn a study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, researchers Rosanna P. Baker and Arturo Casadevall examined fossil evidence from three boundary sections, one in the Denver Basin in Colorado and two in the Williston Basin in North Dakota. Their paper, Fungal proliferation before and after the Cretaceous-Paleogene mass extinction event in North America, documented a sharp increase in fungal remains immediately after the Chicxulub impact. The researchers compared the share of fungal remains among palynomorphs before and after the impact and argued that the fungal spike appeared just after the K/Pg boundary. They noted that this was the first North American record of the bloom and suggested it supported a broader, possibly global, wave of fungal proliferation after major ecosystem collapse.Palynomorphs are microscopic organic remains preserved in sediment, including pollen and spores and the US Geological Survey explains that they can preserve evidence of past environmental changes over millions of years. They show that fungi were present, but not how many living organisms there were. The Denver Basin findings are consistent with earlier evidence from New Zealand and suggest that the post-extinction fungal increase may have occurred across multiple regions, although further evidence is needed to establish how widespread the phenomenon was. The results are consistent with a broader ecosystem response to the extinction.The above-mentioned study also identified a prolonged interval of elevated fungal abundance in the Late Cretaceous, which its abstract dates to roughly 30,000 to 10,000 years before the impact. The authors note that this interval coincided with climatic cooling at the site and with the Poladpur phase of Deccan Traps volcanism in India, but a coincidence in timing does not establish a causal link.Dead vegetation may have favored decomposing fungiDamage to terrestrial ecosystems was brought about by the asteroid impact and its effects. The death of plants and decline in vegetation resulted in accumulation of dead organic matter, which could provide nutrients to some organisms that derive nutrients from decomposition of dead matter. Saprotrophic fungi are decomposers that feed on dead organic matter, including dead plants. The authors say it is likely that abundant decaying biomass after the mass extinction favored saprotrophic fungi, though they could not match the fossil forms to living fungal genera.However, the findings of the researchers were based on fossil records and not on direct estimates of dead biomass available to the fungi. This is an important distinction since an increase in the fossil record of fungi shows a change in the abundance of fungi in the sample sediments, but not necessarily the ecological conditions that caused such a change.Earlier chemical evidence pointed to fungal activityA 2020 paper by Berry in Acta Palaeobotanica, Evidence for fungal proliferation following the Cretaceous/Paleogene mass-extinction event, based on chemostratigraphy in the Raton and Powder River basins, western North America, examined boundary clay in the Raton Basin of Colorado and the Powder River Basin of Wyoming. The paper focuses on the Aib horizon in boundary clay from the Raton and Powder River basins, arguing that Aib is unlikely to be extraterrestrial because impact conditions would have destroyed it.Alpha-aminoisobutyric acid is a chemical compound that is known as Aib in short. The study examined the presence of α-aminoisobutyric acid (Aib) in Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary clay deposits in the Raton Basin of Colorado and the Powder River Basin of Wyoming to investigate evidence of chemical changes associated with the extinction event. The author proposed that this chemical horizon tracked a fungal spike like the one detected in New Zealand. This was indirect evidence of higher fungal activity in the region at the boundary between the two periods, since Aib is a fungal product rather than a fossil. Unlike the above-mentioned study, which focused on fossilized fungi found in North American sediments, the Berry paper based its conclusion on chemical composition. Thus, both studies offer various types of evidence of the increased activity of fungi in the proximity of the extinction event.The fungal bloom was not a single giant organismThe idea that a giant fungus took over forests after the dinosaurs went extinct could be misleading. What the findings entail is the growth in the abundance of microbial parts of fungi and not necessarily the evolution of one single giant fungus that has covered the land. Prototaxites is sometimes raised in discussions of giant fungi, but it lived about 407 million years ago, more than 340 million years before the end-Cretaceous extinction, so it has no bearing on the post-impact fungal bloom.According to a 2026 study published in Science Advances, fossils of Prototaxites taiti from the 407-million-year-old Rhynie chert differ structurally and chemically from known fungi, casting doubt on its classification as a fungus. Some researchers argue that it belongs in an extinct lineage of eukaryotes. Its oddity in form does not mean that there was a giant fungus following the demise of the dinosaurs.Fungi may have played a role in post-extinction ecosystemsThis new information helps scientists better comprehend how these organisms reacted to one of the greatest biological catastrophes on Earth. The ability of fungi to break down organic matter could be useful after the impact and could contribute to the cycling of nutrients in the new ecosystem. The fossil record does not help to prove that fungi became dominant in all ecosystems after the extinction or help to determine their contribution to the recovery of the terrestrial ecosystems. What it does prove is that there was an increased amount of fungal fossils in the studied sediments. Instead of showing how a huge fungus took over the world, the fossil record suggests a wider ecological reaction. In a world where food chains had been disrupted and where organic material was abundant, fungi could have found ideal conditions for survival.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Lula challenges Bolsonaro to release personal records before election
articles.summary: Brazil’s left-wing president says he will release bank, tax, and phone records if right-wing rival will do the same.
articles.body:
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has challenged right-wing candidate Senator Flavio Bolsonaro to release his personal records in the run-up to the second round of the country’s presidential election , in which corruption has emerged as a key issue.

Lula said on Tuesday that he would share his bank, tax and telephone records, along with those of his family, if Bolsonaro would agree to do the same.

“I’m willing to let Brazilians see who the thieves and corrupt people in this country really are. I want to see whether he [Bolsonaro] has the courage to disclose his bank and phone records,” the left-wing president said during a campaign event in Maranhao state.

The call from Lula comes as both campaigns try to navigate the fallout of an explosive corruption scandal involving disgraced banker Daniel Vorcaro that has implicated influential individuals and institutions across Brazil.

While Bolsonaro is the only major presidential candidate with direct links to Vorcaro, the scandal has also hit the country’s Supreme Federal Court, a major target of right-wing ire for sentencing former President Jair Bolsonaro , Flavio’s father, to 27 years in prison for his role in a coup plot after Lula defeated him in 2022.

Concerns about corruption have become a potent issue that the right has sought to capitalise on, a dynamic that Lula has tried to turn to his advantage in the closing weeks of the race.

Worries about US interference have also loomed over the race following a series of interventions by the Trump administration in Brazilian domestic matters, and reports that the US social media giant Meta had taken steps to restrict Lula’s online campaign prompted a legal complaint.

The company told Brazil’s Supreme Court on Tuesday that it has taken steps to ensure equal treatment for both candidates.

Meta added that any automated restrictions on advertising accounts from either campaign would be reviewed within two hours through the second round of voting on Sunday.

The news service AFP reported that Lula would seek to disqualify Bolsonaro’s campaign on the grounds that “algorithmic manipulation” in his favour by Meta, citing an anonymous source.
